My fiance took a tire in for repair and was charged $25 for a mechanic to "remove & patched tire, mounted and re balance" this never happened. The tire was taken in, off the vehicle, and was plugged - the plug was not even trimmed. The dirt on the rim was not even smudged. When I called and spoke to the front desk girl she stated the mechanic made that note so she charged for the patch and to please come back in to straighten it out. My fiance went back and the story changed to it was all her fault and the $10 price difference between the $25 patch repair and the actual $15 plug repair was refunded.....  We will not be back to a place that scams customers.

The bill was approximately $145... the most I've ever paid. On the receipt the mech listed leaks that needed to be fixed totaling $2400! I'm not saying something smells fishy but when I asked the receptionist if the mechanic could show me, she said no one's allowed in the garage. Alarms sounded in my head and I thanked her and left. I circulate with a lot of "car people" , and the most knowledgeable of these (local) car people recommend Alex at Vato's without a pause.

In my dealings with Vato's I have found Alex to be genuinely concerned with my problems, very energetic in efforts to diagnose and most importantly - HONEST.

The staff here rotates out frequently, which is par for most private mechanic shops, but are overall helpful and serious. I haven't seen them try to gauge me, like how other shops will tack on services not explicitly requested. All around just really good service and at a reasonable rate.

Exactly what I needed, no more, no less.

The guy was great and to the point. I was taking in a vehicle to get it checked out before I made my final decision on purchasing it or not and he made me feel confident in my choice.

I took the vehicle in, they got me right in and it took less than an hour. They went through everything very thoroughly and layer it all our for me. There was complete transparency; price listings on parts, labors rates and times for each repair and a full quote to back it all up. He even went through and showed me what I looked like damaged compared to how it should look.

To top it all of, he worked through the list with me to determine the necessities, the needs, and the wants. Plus, a time frame of when to get it all done and not break my bank at the same time.

All in all, it was a pleasure dealing with them and they are now my go to garage.

However, over the years from so much use and abuse, there has been a lot of damage to the trees and other vegetation.

"Compaction" as State Parks calls it, from so many happy feet visiting virtual wilderness, compacts the soil around the roots of trees which exposes their roots.  Then the trees die and blow over in the wind.  Then more trees are exposed and blow down.  This is a cascading effect.  Then forest fires rage through as natures way of clearing the debris and restoring the forest.

Mc Hough Creek is A GREAT place to begin UNPRECEDENTED collaboration between Alaska State Parks, Chugach National Forest and those who know and love Mc Hough Creek and Forest.  This collaboration is a way for people and government to work together for virtual benefit.

Otherwise, Mc Hough Creek may continue to become more and more degraded.

Warm water, friendly crowds, parking isn't free but you get what you pay for and it's well well worth it
Great campsite. Water not the best for swimming though due to soft bottom, a few leeches... Stay in the boat?
Nice lake to go camping or boating. Quiet tent camping is kept separate from motor home camping. Can be busy on a sunny day. Clean out houses.
Great place to camp in the fall.
Good facilities. Nice boat ramp. Fishing was good.

I always enjoy coming here. It is quiet, pristine and folks fishing or not fishing are uneventful, quiet, enjoying an Alaskan pasttime, subsistence activity, while respecting of others present, who are like minded and in tune with Alaskan outdoors we grew up with.
Great place to walk your dog take wildlife pictures and if you can handle the cold there's dollies in there👍
It's neat.  Not overcrowded when it's not fishing season.
Beautiful area to enjoy a nice quick walk during the winter months. We got to see a lot of Eagles flying over the river which was an added bonus.
A popular place to give your best shot at landing a big fish. Be prepped for near combat style fishing if you're after the elusive King salmon.
Nice little one sided lake. A load of abandoned classical cars on the edge of a portion of the lake. Definitely not good for a hike. It is however a great fishing spot.

Beautiful place to fish with the family...there is even enough room for being socially distanced with multiple families. The people fishing there are always friendly. It's clean for the most part and there is handicapped parking close to the water and there are outhouses!
Amazing place to catch salmon and enjoy the beautiful mountains in Alaska
A beautiful scene for a winter family photo shoot with Britta.

We stopped for a break to strech our legs after a few hours in the car. The weather was cooperative Sunny with a smattering of clouds and a nice refreshing breeze for the warm day it was. We walked some of trails and talked to some of the people fishing. I also had to to take some pictures.
Beautiful trail & Trail. The old cars buried into the side of the trial is awesome!
Went with a Cub Scout Den Meeting.  This is an awesome place to visit in early winter

This is a nice parking area with restrooms and some decent fishing at times. I used to fish this place 30+ years ago and had some good times and good fishing. This is more like a ship creek or Russian but in a smaller scale.
Easy access. Fishing was slow but we picked up a nice silver. Clean facilities and well maintained.
Nice very easy walk every can do it.
It's a good place to go fishing or just spend some time exploring the old junk cars, and the trails.

Great place to fish for people ages 1 to 100!
Nicely maintained, & filled with friendly Alaskan families 🙂
A nice area, well maintained.  I enjoyed the trails.  The views and you can fish from an easily accessible area.

Lots of fishermen and women when we arrived; this place looks like a pretty popular spot to catch these scaley, sneaky devils. Still, it offers some amount of seclusion alongside the river bank, though fair warning: it gets super muddy after rain. Get your boots, get rid of not wanting to be dirty, and CAST.

I think this is a great place to fish. There were a lot of salmon activity when I was there and there isn't a parking fee! It's a beautiful location where two rivers meet. The trail race is silty water so make sure you use bright colors if your trying to get the fish's attention. I'll definately be back.
So pretty along the frosty trees and the ice blue water. Will do it again this summer when the trees are bloomed with leafs.
This place has some fish; gotta be a good catch them.
Decent fishing, lots of parking, great views
Gorgeous aqua blue water, little mosquitoes,  but caught zero fish.
it's a very relaxing place. never caught anything but it's pretty and the kids like it.

I took the tour to one of the most majestic glaciers that I’ve ever seen. And the sad part is, the Columbia Glacier is also one of the fastest shrinking glaciers in Alaska, and the world. The tour is worth every penny! They take you to the glaciers, and you’ll see a whole lot of other natural scenery and wildlife on the way: icebergs, forested mountains, waterfalls, sea lions, puffins, whales, sea otters, eagles, etc. It’s a must-do when you’re in Valdez. The served food was delicious, and the staff are polite, knowledgeable, and attentive!

Wow! Incredible! Crew went out of their way to make it awesome! Very nice boat,  very informative! Do yourself a favor and take the 8 hour cruise! ( unfortunately,  all the sealife are on my other camera......sea otters,  seal lions, humpback whale putting on a show,  puffins...)

This was my first time on this cruise even though I have lived here for 9 years. I took the 6 hour Colimbia glacier. I wish I would have done this earlier. We(my 4.5 year old and I) were showing an out of state friend a beautiful piece of the state. The day before the cruise was gorgeous, but the day of the cruise was rainy and socked in. I made sure to being rain pants and coats, as well as plenty of warm fleece gear. It was cool out, and it gets cold around the glacier. They have  a recent captain's report of what they saw on their site. They had been seeing whales, sea lions, seals, and puffins among other animals most days. Unfortunately due to bad weather they weren't able to go near that area. We still saw plenty of otters, mountain goats, porpoises, surfscooters, and other sea birds. They served warm clam chowder, bagel and oreos for lunch. They also have minestrone soup for those who don't want clam chowder. I will definitely go on another cruise of theirs.

Very good excursion.  Saw lots of sea life and Columbia Glacier.  Large, comfortable boat. Good food, especially the chowder.
Sail out of Valdez Alasks
Amazing. Highly recommend for anyone to take their family when they come to Alaska

I have been on these cruises several times and always encourage any visitors to try and make it if they can.  The price is not too bad and the chance to see some of the most beautiful scenery in the world is priceless.  If you are blessed to go on a clear day you will be in for a lifetime memory experience.

My Husband and I are newly weds. We decided to take their tour while on our Honeymoon and I'll tell you what??

Went on a tour with Stan Stevens in Valdez, AK.

The ONLY excellent thing about this tour was the fact my Husband and I were together. That was FANTASTIC and I can't complain.
Highly recommended glacier and wildlife cruise.  Best tour in Valdez, great staff and beautifully kept vessels.
Beautiful views! Captain went out of her way to get the best views. Saw a bear, whale, seals, otters, and a puffin. Worth the money. Would do it again
Loved the cruise! Excellent food and the crew was great. We saw many otters, seals, and sea lions
Very comfortable way to see so much of ak in half a day. Well earned reputation for consistency, service, and wildlife sootting

Great way to explore Prince William sound and see the wildlife that is abundant in the area with several Cruise options available in half-day and full-day trips. Great family run business with long history in Alaska. Boat captains are knowledgeable and friendly and ships crew make you feel at home.

Good boat captain which sees every little jellyfish. Really friendly staff! Definitely much better than the more expensive Kenaifjords. com cruise in Seward, where you can see the half of this tour. Free coffee and water (nice add on :-)

A spectacular cruise with great close up views of a spectacular glacier. Saw whales, seals, a moose swimming from island to island too many species to mention in a short review. After taking both the Seward tour and this one I would have to agree that this tour is by far the best one there is. If you get a chance view the pictures I also posted to give you just a little taste of this cruise.

The catamaran was very clean. The captain waa knowledgeable and the staff in the boat were pleasant. Free unlimited coffee and tea on board. The dinner was delicious. It was clam chowder. We saw whales, murre, cormorants, puffins, sea lions and of course the tidewater glacier. It was a great adventure.

Cheaper glacier cruise compared to Seward, and bigger/better glacier too. Friendly staff, delicious chowder for lunch. Captain gives a great tour and went over and beyond by providing extra tour of wildlife after viewing  Columbia Glacier. Highly recommend over Seward options.
.a good trip, Captain was very knowledgeable. Crew very helpful.
Very friendly, very good looking staff. Best cruise in town, possibly the world. Can't imagine a better day.
It was a great cruise. We went to the Meares    glacier and saw quite a lot of wildlife. The ship was very comfortable and much bigger than the other cruise ships in Valdez
Fun adventure trip. We saw sea lions, whales, and otters. Then we picked our way through an ice field to watch the glacier calve and kayaks dart around.
Amazing captain. Tried to show us so much and was really into everything.
Alaska is so magical and this cruise fuels the enchantment. A must Do trip!
Nice, perfect to get out big towns. Peace and silence, cleaned places..and big mountains to see..and admired the the hard working people in the cold weather.
Wonderful crew, very knowledgeable and helpful.
Take the ride. It is well worth it and the views are wonderful. Well worth the money to see the glacier
Great coffee. Great food. Friendly service. A great little place in Talkeetna.
I cannot describe how delicious the sandwich I got at this restaurant was along with the cookies and the drink I thought I was in heaven!
Vegan sandwich might have been the best sandwich of my life
Take out only due to virus. Order inside. Many tempting offers. We had a variety and all were very good. Take a break here.
Fresh baked breads and a large unique menu.  Open year round!
I go in here with a plan to buy just a sandwich and a latte, and my plan never works because I can't resist all the gorgeous yummy goods available!
Some of the best breakfast choices we had during our one-month trip to Alaska. Even my picky son loved the food. Cool atmosphere, chill environment.
A Talkeetna landmark. Awesome baked goods and pizza. The oatmeal raisin cookies were wonderful and I got tons of them for a great price.

Coffee was decent. Chai tea cookie was good. The cafe features Birch syrup which is fun if you're new around AK. I LOVE that they had compostable coffee lids that are also made locally in Alaska! So cool. They were quite busy and started running out of tables by the time we left, so if you're going at peak coffee hour be prepared to get your coffee to go. It looked like they had a really delicious food menu but I didn't get to try any this time around.
Love this place great breakfast and coffee....pastries too.
An exceptional experience.  Will be coming back again.

A great place to stop and enjoy something to eat, especially for breakfast! The staff was friendly and helpful. There’s plenty of parking out front and there are signs to identify when to pull off the main road.

Nice breakfast stop off. Greeted by gorgeous aromas of bakery, the rather lovely serving girl with unusual pearcings, was friendly and cute. I ordered a breakfast with additional cheese, egg and bacon... It was nice enough, but without the adds it'd have been slim pickings. I'd recommend it if only to check out the locals and work out whether having your cheeks pierced hurts as much as I think it did.
Friendly staff, great homemade bread. Sweet and savory pastries.
Great coffee, very good breakfast options made from local garden ingredients, good service.
Stopped here on my way from Denali and wasn’t disappointed. Really enjoyed the muffuletta.
This place was great. Lots of different food choices. They have wi fi. Friendly service, not fast but good food
The sandwiches here are good and I would give them 5 stars but the attitude of the staff could use some work. The young lady behind the counter could be a little more friendly.

Another server came to help and she was wonderful. The food however was just meh. It's a cute place though. We found a table and it was quiet.
What a fun place!  My Wife and I really enjoyed the atmosphere as well as the fantastic wholesome food.  These people genuinely care.
Their pastry croissants are delightful
Delicious healthy foods desserts and breads,  I am so in love with this place!! One of my favorite cafes.
Breakfast was delicious! The Tea selection was great. I had the local honey cinnamon toast and I just want more.

Hell yeeeaaahhh. Best coffee and breakfast downtown! Check em out for sure. Staff is great. Awesome art on the walls every month. (I bought some). Oh ya, great sandwiches and ICE CREAM!
Amazing homemade food, wonderful atmosphere and incomparable customer service. I had the ham and brie panini and vegetable minestrone soup.
Really liked the interior of the café. Service was good. They don't have much additions to their menu; basic and tastes great!
Excellent options and their handmade cupcakes are incredible!

Really good coffee, excellent service, great atmosphere. Only issue is parking. Street paid parking only, so be prepared to drive around a bit to find a spot. I was lucky and got a spot right out front at noon.
Kids like the ice cream here. The "Baby Moose" is a great portion with a great price for young ones. Is off the path sonewhat for downtiwn, but never a long wait!

And if I remember correctly they offered free WiFi.

Stoped in for some coffee that came out okay. I liked the live music and friendly staff. They have snack such as you would find at any coffee shop. Worth a stop to check out if you are in the area. One more thing they have out door seating on the side walk that i wish more places did.
Fun local spot, good lunch options, great service. Close to water viewpoint. I had half a chicken ceaser salad and it was fresh and very good.
Always a good place for a meal, snack, cup of coffee. Staff are always friendly the atmosphere is relaxing and the food is great.
A cold stone creamery but slightly better prices

This is a consistently good place to come. I really like the vegetarian breakfast burritos they carry,  which are healthier than burritos I've found other places while still tasting good, and the espresso coffee is well-prepared. They have daily espresso drink specials, which are unique. Prices are competitive for downtown Anchorage- burritos are ~$6.00, 16oz Americano runs around $3.
Great little eatery. Excellent drinks, ladies working were easy going and friendly, and from being from the 505, their version of green chili stew was pretty dang good. Will definitely be going back.
Great atmosphere and friendly service. The prices and selection are excellent. I enjoyed the ice cream and art work on display.
Comfortable place to sit and have coffee, They also have ice cream! Wheelchair accessible entrance.

This is a really great place to eat and chill. It has that calm coffeehouse feel with great Café-style food to match! Smiling staff and affordable prices makes this a great choice for anyone looking to catch a quick bite and some coffee in a quiet environment.
Great service. The owner is reslly nice. Good food
Delicious food, ice cream too. Prices are great for Anchorage which is a not very cheap place. And there is free WiFi.
Great food.
Delicious sandwich and salad. Nice people!
Love this place, coffee is good, good is great, employees are super friendly and I love going here.
Always smells so good in there.  Staff is helpful and fun.

I use it as a place to work, and the food and coffee is very good, but the atmosphere is not my style. Seems to be run by college students, service is not great. They have a bathroom, which can be hard to find downtown. WiFi available, but pretty slow.

This one is tricky. Its a ice cream shop, that also serves lunch and coffee. I dont drink coffee so i cant review. However their icecream is pricey (probabaly because its downtown) and its nothing fantastic. Lunch sandwiches are the same thing, pricey and nothing fancy.

Resurrect Art Coffee House is always a MUST do stop for myself whenever I’m in Seward. The staff are always friendly and pleasant! The coffee house is an historic building that pumps out some of the best espresso beverages in the state (IMO) and there is always wonderful artwork and Alaskan literature to peruse through while one is waiting for their order to come out. If you’re looking for a chill environment to read and drink coffee, or maybe you’re a tourist wishing to see the best of Seward, make a stop at “The Rez”.
Great coffee place with treats. Day old treats were only $0.93. Kids loved the hot chocolate with whipped cream and sprinkles.
Cute shop with a dog! The ambiance is great and the coffee is delicious. There is now a to go window as well
A little too "Liberal" for my taste. Decent coffee, but a waste of a good Church.

Great space and smooth latte, open all year.  The loft upstairs is a magical, cozy space with lots of light (in the summer) and the walls are filled with art. There is even a little thrift shop corner.
Great coffee in Seward. Very ecclectic and service was great.
Great coffee and baked goods to start our day! All in a repurposed historic church.
Our daily stop. Coffee was always on point and quickly served. We loved the old house and feel of the establishment. Look around at local art and pottery, we found several really awesome pieces.
Very cozy coffee house. Beautiful view from the second floor arctic.

On our trip to Alaska, we were in Seward for 3 days. The whole town was charming, but Resurrect Art Coffee House was our favorite stop.
We visited right before winter, and found ourselves with very few options for restaurants that were actually open. It worked out, though, because we found Resurrect Art and went multiple times in the three days.
Coffee, mocha, chai, and cocoa were DELICIOUS. Staff was friendly. Atmosphere was great... and the little upstairs area was so homey and beautiful, I could've stayed forever.

Their selection of goods by local artisans was wonderful. We picked up some jewelry, pins, and stickers that turned out to be our favorite momentos from our whole 10 days in Alaska.

It is amazing, use to be a church.  LOVE sitting up in the old belltower.  The coffee ☕ is delicious and wonderful food options. There's lots of locally made product such as cards, jewelry, clothing, art & more for sale.  The outside garden is a nice place to sip you beverage of choice.

Good coffee and breakfast
Nice place to enjoy and buy local craft gifts
I loved everything about this place.  The location.  The art.  The staff.  And, the hot chocolate.  Definitely a place to visit!

Fantastic venue for coffee, art, and relaxation in a renovated church while maintaining an original venue feeling. The coffee is strong, hot, inexpensive, and luscious! The staff is friendly and the patrons inviting. Definitely come and enjoy. We might drive down from Anchorage just for coffee...

Nice atmosphere with cool stuff to look at. Busy and trendy. The goat cheese wrap was filling and tasty. The Americano was $4 and exceptional. The smell is lovely coffee all the way. Best coffee shop in Seward.

A perfect place to have a coffee. My favorite is the Almond Joy Coffee. Run into locals, get to pet the beautiful owners dog. Lovely artist work displayed. Great places to sit around the shop to become inspired.

One of the only coffee places open in the winter, this is a great spot for locals! Very cool vibes, and always great art work on the walls that rotate out frequently. The loft area is the best seat in town, with beautiful views overlooking downtown and Resurrection Bay. Only downside is cost, as it can get pricey. However, you can get a better cup of coffee for the same price as Starbucks, so while you're in town, be sure to stop by!

Beautiful, cozy coffee shop in a rehabilitated church building featuring loads of artwork and plenty of seating options plus free WiFi.

I had the mocha which was just okay. Tasted more like chocolate milk than coffee. Next day I got the cold Brew which was much better. It came out of a box but really I don't care as long as it is good. I've seen that same box at Safeway and it's an Alaskan roaster.

Strangely the only history information I found was in the only restroom they have (there was a line when I went to use it). I suggest you enjoy a leisurely bathroom break to read it (and might I suggest to the owners that they put that info on the outside of the door so you can read it while you're waiting)
Breakfast is just sugar and wheat stuffs. Not my palate . Nice environment to chill
Great atmosphere!  Cool place! Coffee, Tea, art for sale from local artists!
The coffee is absolutely fantastic!
I nice place to relax, have coffee and see some of the local creativity.

Hard to imagine a more unique coffee shop. Housed in a century-old church, you look through gothic windows at snow capped peaks out one side and out into the ocean from the other. Add to that a hip, artsy vibe, giant, cozy wood stove, and the friendliest baristas you'll ever meet and, well sir, nirvana awaits. Well- priced for Seward (or Anchorage, for that matter). Plan a few extra minutes to sit in the balcony and enjoy views of Resurrection Bay and chat with friendly locals for tips on how to best enjoy the city.
Great coffee, smoked salmon schmear bagel was awesome! Loved the view from the steeple.

An amazing coffee house with great coffee and enjoyable local art for sale.  The old church at the base of mount marathon makes this a wonderful place to have a cup of joe with a good book you have been wanting to read.
We went for the brewery but found it to be closed on certain days. Luckily the bar downstairs was fun! But it was cash only. Fun dive bar.
Thank to Rick the owner and Rachel the bartender this place became one of the best places in town for a club entertainment in the Interior!!
Interesting dive bar downstairs and brewery upstairs.

Talon makes GREAT beer and rivals the best beer in the state! Yes, it’s inside – upstairs – of the old Midnite Mine bar, but it’s a completely different experience. They also have some other Alaska craft beers on tap, have house-made sangria, some select spirits and craft cocktails. AND, they are open later than any brewery in town:) A true nano brewery that is just feet away from the cozy bar. I always look forward to the next beer they cook up!

Great atmosphere for a downtown bar. As a local, one of my places to go. Drinks are cheap, and STRONG. Certainly one or the best bang for your buck places in Fairbanks. Pool, foosball, and darts are here for use, and a fantastic atmosphere for anyone willing to walk .5 miles from their hotel downtown!
Great beer, and great staff!
Love this place on warm nights, sitting outside on the deck! They also have a micro brewery upstairs. Check them out!
That's a cool little bar and a cool little brewery
Fun place
The new brewery in town has great beers. I wish his system was a bit bigger so we could enjoy the flavors more
My favorite stop in Fairbanks, and now they have a brewery! Only to make it better. Great atmosphere and people. A+

great little dive bar go every Sunday for darts

Very nice little park, well kept trails but not so urbanized that it feels like a walk in the city. Definitely bring bear spray or self defense items if owned, as wildlife and Anchorages growing community of criminals can and have been seen out here. In the early morning through to early evening, the park and trails are fairly well populated with other walkers and families so you’re probably pretty safe out here, gauge activity by the number of open parking spaces and act accordingly. Be safe out there fellow Trail Blazers!
Good place for taking photos...
Love the park...its too bad the illegal campers are there. Lots of trash. I can't understand why people are so trashy.

This place has good parking. The trail around the lake is great. The park is connected to the ..... Newly paved Campbell creek trail. The lake has small trout, Campbell creek has some salmon to view and try for with rod and reel.
It's a nice little lake and the trails I've been on are ok. On a good day you may see light wild life activity - otters, beavers, eagles. It's a good place to walk your dog.

Great hiking trails around the lake. Very close to town. Excellent trout fishing. I have heard of leeches in this lake, but have not seen any this spring. My dog loves to swim here. No problems yet. Only downside is that you will find sketchy druggies hanging out here very early morning (when I fish). Mid-day and afternoon, this lake is super fun, but busy. River runs right next to it to the North.
Great place for fishing, walking, biking with a nice wide lighted trail, picnic tables, and benches.  Limited parking during popular times.
Gorgeous park along the trail. Stocked with fish and able to be kayaked on
Very nice lake with a bike trail all the way around.

Its a scenic park with lots of people walking or bike riding up an down cambell creek which has miles of  wilderness to explore. It is always a treat visiting this local treasure. Get your kids out or take your dog along. Good times by all.
Ended up here after floating down Campbell Creek. Really fun.
Small fishing lake surrounded by homes and businesses. Lots of picnic areasbenches and a main picnic pavilion on the west end.

It's a pretty small area that leads to more. The main attractions are the circular trails that breaks off into others and the fishing pond here. The fishing pond here is stocked with trout. There are also off-pavement trails that have some nice scenery.
Great for short or long walks, since it does connect all around. Cute little lake to walk around that usually has an abundance of ducks and such.

Fantastic, although, can be hard to find (which can add to it's charm)... Not too big and not on a main road... Don't bother fishing... And, yes, there are life vests there, but no life guard.  We took a raft out and drifted.  There were some flat boarders there as well.  Tables are there and there are trails and people walk their dogs...

A decent place with decent scenery where you can go for decent walks and decent bike rides to many decent parts of town.  There's a lake and different paths with streams and places to go fishing or take your dogs for a walk.  Not as impressive as some of the other trails around town but it's a peaceful place to clear your mind if nothing else.

I have going to this lake for 40 years now and it's still just as beautiful as ever! It's a great place for kids and pets and a good swimming and fishing hole too! You can go out on kayaks or a canoe and floats as well. I have always loved this lake. We used to call I it C street lake back in the 70's before it was ever named Taku lake.
My dog said this is his fav. They just put up a notice to get homeless out of here so that's always nice too
I love going here and rock hunting.

Improvements to the trail around the lake since we been here last. Lots of beaver activity. Loons and other birds can be seen.
Beautiful little getaway in Anchorage with nice walking trails.

The lake itself is accessible on all sides, which makes it easy to toss a kayak in a float around on a nice sunny afternoon.

However, the fishing is sub par compared to other locally stocked lakes and I would not recommend swimming this lake (or any Anchorage lake for that matter).

Grassy hills, open fields and nearby local breweries just down the street are added benefits to this local park. Don't overlook it at winter-time either!
great man made pond
Always fun taking the boys here to catch fish! Friendly people. Well kept. Nice trails.
This place is a little taste of sanity on our way home from town. Right outside the craziness of fairbanks it's quiet and clean. All the employees are 10/10.

So happy about this new gas station!! Friendly staff & very helpful! Free coffee in the mornings!

Place is super convenient and prices are fair. We got got donuts that were old.

We were renting a cabin at Miller's Landing through Airbnb.  They called to let us know they offer tours so we took them up on it.  We scheduled a full day kayak tour. It was nice to be on property as we had to meet at the dock at 5:30am.

When we arrived we met Chris our guide for the day.  We were the only kayakers on a boat of fishermen.  We had a 2 hour ride out to Northwestern Fjord.  We were going one bay over from where they usually kayak to accommodate the people fishing.

They dropped us off on the rocky beach.  The boat has a gangway that lowers down on the bow so we just had to walk off onto the beach.  My daughter and I were happy we wore our rubber boots so we could just plod through the water.  They quickly unloaded the kayaks and all the gear we will need for the day.

Chris quickly went to work setting up our double kayaks while we ran around taking pictures of the amazing scenery.  After a quick review of safety and paddling technique he dragged us to the water and sent us off into the water.  We started paddling through the pristine bay and it was a surreal experience. Pictures do not do the amazing beauty justice.

We paddled about 4 miles and made a quick stop to adjust the foot pedals for the rudder and just take a quick stretch.  We had also dressed for a cool paddle and the temperature and the sun were making it quite warm so we peeled off a layer of clothes.  We continued to paddle through the floating icebergs and had many curious seals popping up to check us out.  We also had a whale sighting about 200 feet off the bow of our kayak.

We approached the foot of the Northwestern glacier and could hear the glacier calving.  The blue ice glistened in the sun and we pulled over to the rocky beach to have our lunch.  Chris laid out sandwiches, chips, and snacks.  There were some large ice chunks on land from high tide so we went over for photo ops with them and the glacier in the background.

With our bellies full we headed back out on the water to paddle over to Ogive (pronounced Ojai) glacier.  The base of it had disconnected from the Harding ice field above so it is brown and old looking.  It is super tall and hard to tell scale from the pictures.  We pulled up on the rocky coast next to Anchor Glacier that is very close to Ogive.  Chris had brought hot chocolate and his stove thinking, like us, that it was going to be cold.  We opted for the water instead since the sun was still shining bright and keeping us warm.

From here we had 1.5 hours to paddle 4 miles to the extraction point.  Unfortunately, after a very calm flat morning on the water, the head winds had kicked up and were now making the waves crash over the bow of our kayaks.  It made for some difficult paddling for the end of the day.  We muscled through but were exhausted by the time we got to the beach.  We had been paddling since 9 am with our couple of stops and we pulled in to the final stop at 4pm. The route we took is also a 3 night camping trip which would be a phenomenal way to experience all that this Fjord has to offer on a much more relaxed experience.

We waited for the boat to come pick us up and reflected on our amazing day.  Chris is such a hard worker.  He pulled us in and pushed us off of each stop all day. He was a wealth of information about the surrounding area the water, glaciers and animals.  He even gave us a great suggestion for dinner later that night.

When we got back on the boat for our 2 hour ride back to Miller's Landing we all fell asleep.  The combination of the early morning and 14 miles of paddling had gotten the best of us.  Chance, is one of the owners of Miller's Landing and was our boat captain.  He grew up in the area and is really interesting to talk to. He is very concerned about providing a positive experience and making his customers happy.  I highly recommend you do a kayak or fishing tour with Miller's Landing and explore all that this amazing area of the world has to offer.

I know, I know -- I'm the minority opinion here, because no one in our party of four found anything endearing about the Fortress of the Bear. What sounds like a compelling story -- cubs, saved from euthanasia by placing them in a walled containment facility -- struck us as the result of good intentions gone awry. While closely-cropped images on the facility's website showcase the animals, in person, we couldn't not see the dreary environment, with trash floating in the water and busted tired strewn across the landscape. The bears may love it -- but we left depressed and a little sad. Not recommended.
